rv.q: "The Full Monty," if you see it done right as is the case here, strips away more than you might think.
It is simply a joy in every way; if you love musicals, you should see it.
Paramount has done it again and their new season is off to a wild start with this R-rated musical.
Add in a terrific cast and you’ve got a winner from top to bottom!

I can report that the big-hearted, deliciously naughty revival playing through Oct. 6 at Aurora’s Paramount Theatre does, courtesy of the brief, artfully conceived finale from director Jim Corti and lighting designer Heather Gilbert, who uses backlighting to excellent effect.

Rebecca Hurd as Pam, Jerry’s ex, Jared David Michael Grant as his best pal, Dave, and Liz Pazik as Jeanette, the brassy showbiz vet who just shows up with her piano to help “Hot Metal” find their beat and their joy, are particular standouts in this meat-and-potatoes heart-warmer of a show.
Under the skilled leadership and direction of Jim Corti who has put together a wonderful cast of players, you get to see "The Full Monty" as never before!
With superb direction, stellar performances, and a production that radiates joy and sincerity, The Full Monty is the definition of a feel-good musical.

cn.t: Critics praise this timely, heartfelt production for its sharp direction and moving exploration of masculinity and self-esteem, finding it both bawdy fun and surprisingly poignant beneath the comic strip-tease premise.
